doc.title: Junior Mance Part II interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 18, 1999 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Adjunct faculty union wins raise and benefits
summary: The adjunct teachers' union campaign won raises, pension and health insurance; other New School programs are now following.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: I understand they just had some dealings with the union or something?

Yeah. It worked out. I had misgivings, but they were able to pull it off. Because being adjunct it was hard to get the things they were asking for, but we got them. Yeah, we got a raise in salary. But the main thing they were campaigning for was benefits, pension, health insurance and all that. We got it all.
Wow. Maybe I should send your team up to where I work.
You know what they were the first ones in the City and I understand that a lot of the other programs like ours are investigating it.
Yeah, they’re going to sit up and take notice now.

In fact there’s a couple in the New School, they’re not music programs, but they have adjunct professors and adjunct teachers, and they’re going after it. They’ve hired our lawyers, and asking advice, like from our team, from the union people.
